whyEn: Exam weight 2/3, but this is a 124-page chapter that shows up everywhere: written exam fracture-classification questions, and two full practical stations (isolated femur fracture with traction splint, and unstable pelvis with binding). The chapter's real content is a decision tree — which deformed limb gets one gentle realignment attempt, which fracture gets a traction splint and by how many pounds, which pelvis gets bound and how, and which joint injury is a true emergency because of what runs next to it. Lock in the numbers: blood loss by fracture site, traction weight percentages, pelvic-binder landmarks, and the BC-specific pain ladder that has zero opioids in it.
whyZh: 考试权重 2/3，但这是一章 124 页的大部头，笔试和实操站都会反复出现：骨折分类是笔试常客，实操站更是直接有两整站——孤立性股骨骨折配牵引夹板、骨盆不稳定配骨盆固定带。这一章真正的内容是一套决策树：哪种畸形肢体能做一次轻柔复位、哪种骨折该上牵引夹板、牵引重量怎么算、哪种骨盆该绑、怎么绑、哪种关节伤是因为紧邻的血管神经而成为真正的急症。要死记的数字：各骨折部位的估计失血量、牵引重量百分比、骨盆固定带的解剖标志，以及 BC 版本里完全不含阿片类药物的镇痛阶梯。

sections.titleEn: Introduction and Anatomy of the Musculoskeletal System
sections.titleZh: 引言与肌肉骨骼系统解剖生理

points.en: In Canada, musculoskeletal complaints drive roughly 6 million hospital visits a year — more than any other single cause — and about 1 in 7 Canadians will experience some form of musculoskeletal impairment, costing billions in missed work and school. Unintentional falls are the leading mechanism, followed by motor vehicle collisions; 70-80% of multisystem trauma patients have at least one musculoskeletal injury on top of everything else.
points.zh: 在加拿大，肌肉骨骼相关主诉每年造成约 600 万人次就医——超过任何单一病因；大约每 7 个加拿大人里就有 1 人会经历某种肌骨功能障碍，因缺勤缺课造成数十亿医疗成本。意外跌落是头号致伤机制，其次是车祸；70%-80% 的多系统创伤病人身上都合并至少一处肌骨损伤。

points.en: Musculoskeletal injury is rarely a direct threat to life, but it is a leading cause of short- or long-term disability — prompt splinting and analgesia shorten that disability window. However dramatic the deformity looks, resist the pull toward the limb before you've cleared life threats: airway, breathing, and circulation always come first.
points.zh: 肌骨损伤本身很少直接威胁生命，却是造成短期乃至长期残疾的主要原因——及时上夹板、给镇痛能缩短这段失能期。但不管畸形看着多吓人，都不要在排除生命威胁之前就一头扎向肢体：气道、呼吸、循环永远排在前面。

points.en: Beyond support, posture, movement, and organ protection, the skeleton performs hematopoiesis — manufacturing red cells, white cells, and platelets from stem cells in the red marrow. In adults this happens mainly in the sternum, ribs, vertebral bodies, pelvis, and the proximal femur and humerus, so an injury near one of these sites can be a marker for a deeper problem than the fracture itself.
points.zh: 骨骼除了支撑、维持姿势、协助运动和保护脏器外，还承担造血功能——在红骨髓中由干细胞不断生成红细胞、白细胞和血小板。成人的红骨髓主要分布在胸骨、肋骨、椎体、骨盆以及股骨和肱骨近端，所以这些部位附近受伤，可能提示比骨折本身更深层的问题。

points.en: The skeleton has 206 bones in two divisions. The axial skeleton (skull, 33 vertebrae — 7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 fused sacral, 4 fused coccygeal — ribs, sternum) forms the body's central axis; the appendicular skeleton (pectoral girdle, pelvic girdle, and the upper/lower extremity bones) hangs off it.
points.zh: 骨骼共 206 块，分两部分。中轴骨（颅骨、33 块脊椎骨——7 颈椎、12 胸椎、5 腰椎、5 块融合骶椎、4 块融合尾椎——加上肋骨与胸骨）构成身体中轴；附肢骨（肩带、骨盆带以及上下肢骨）挂在中轴骨上。

points.en: Pectoral girdle = 2 scapulae + 2 clavicles; the slender S-shaped clavicle struts the shoulder up but is very exposed, making it one of the most commonly fractured bones. The humerus meets the scapula proximally and the radius/ulna distally at the elbow; because the radius (thumb side) and ulna (little-finger side) run parallel like a ring, breaking one commonly breaks the other too.
points.zh: 肩带 = 2 块肩胛骨 + 2 块锁骨；细长的 S 形锁骨像支架一样把肩关节撑起来，但也因此非常暴露，是最常骨折的骨骼之一。肱骨近端接肩胛骨，远端在肘关节接桡尺骨；桡骨（拇指侧）和尺骨（小指侧）并行排列如同一个环，断一根另一根常常也跟着断。

points.en: The hand has three bone groups: carpals (the scaphoid is the classic FOOSH — fall-on-outstretched-hand — fracture), metacarpals, and phalanges (more often injured by crush mechanisms, e.g. a car door). Memory aids: a supinated hand can hold a cup of SOUP; you steer your CAR(pal) with your hands and walk through TAR(sal) with your feet.
points.zh: 手部有三组骨：腕骨（跌倒手撑地即 FOOSH 时最经典受伤的是舟状骨）、掌骨、指骨（更常见于挤压伤，如被车门夹到）。助记：手掌旋后（supinate）时能端起一碗汤（SOUP）；用手驾驶 CAR（腕骨 carpal），用脚走过 TAR（跗骨 tarsal）。

points.en: The pelvic ring is three fused bones (ischium, ilium, pubis = the innominate bone) joined posteriorly to the sacrum at the sacroiliac joints and anteriorly to each other at the pubic symphysis — both very tough, near-immobile joints, which is exactly why the ring is normally so strong and stable. The femur's ball-shaped head fits the acetabulum via the femoral neck; the tibia (shin, exposed to direct blows) and fibula (not part of the knee joint, but forms the lateral malleolus) make up the lower leg.
points.zh: 骨盆环由三块融合骨（坐骨、髂骨、耻骨=髋骨）构成：后方经骶髂关节连接骶骨，前方经耻骨联合彼此相连——两处关节都极为坚韧、几乎不能活动，这正是骨盆环平时如此坚固稳定的原因。股骨头经股骨颈嵌入髋臼；胫骨（小腿前侧，直接暴露于撞击）和腓骨（不参与膝关节，但构成外踝）组成小腿。

points.en: The foot has tarsals (the calcaneus, or heel bone, is the largest and is classically fractured by an axial load — jumping/falling and landing on the feet), metatarsals, and phalanges. Bone shapes overall: long (femur, humerus, tibia, fibula, radius, ulna, metacarpals, metatarsals, phalanges), short (carpals, tarsals), flat (sternum, ribs, scapulae, skull), irregular (vertebrae, mandible), and round/sesamoid (the patella is the largest example, embedded in a tendon to act as a pulley).
points.zh: 足部有跗骨（跟骨最大，从高处跳落或坠落双脚着地的轴向负荷是其经典致伤机制）、跖骨、趾骨。骨骼形状总览：长骨（股骨、肱骨、胫骨、腓骨、桡骨、尺骨、掌骨、跖骨、指/趾骨）、短骨（腕骨、跗骨）、扁骨（胸骨、肋骨、肩胛骨、颅骨）、不规则骨（椎骨、下颌骨）、圆/籽骨（髌骨是最大的例子，嵌于肌腱内起滑轮作用）。

points.en: A long bone has three regions — diaphysis, epiphysis, metaphysis — and grows via the growth plate (physis), present only in children and closed by adulthood; a growth-plate fracture in a child can affect that bone's future growth. Articular surfaces are covered by articular cartilage (a cushion); the rest of the bone is covered by periosteum, which contains the nerve endings responsible for fracture pain plus the vessels needed for repair. Inside, the medullary canal is lined by endosteum and holds yellow (fatty) marrow in adults, fed by the nutrient artery.
points.zh: 长骨分骨干、骨骺、干骺端三个区域，靠儿童期特有的生长板（骺板）生长，成年后闭合；儿童生长板骨折可能影响该骨未来的生长。关节面覆盖关节软骨（缓冲垫）；骨的其余部分覆盖骨膜——骨膜内的神经末梢正是骨折剧痛的来源，同时也含有负责修复的血管。骨内部的骨髓腔内衬骨内膜，成人内含黄（脂肪）骨髓，由营养动脉供血。

points.en: Bone density starts declining after age 35 and accelerates after menopause (loss of the bone-forming hormone estrogen); the result, osteoporosis, means hip, spine, and wrist fractures can occur with minimal or no trauma. If straightening an injured limb for splinting meets resistance or increases pain — common in osteoarthritic elderly patients — stop and splint it in the position found instead of forcing it.
points.zh: 骨密度在 35 岁后开始下降，绝经后（促骨形成的雌激素流失）加速下降；由此产生的骨质疏松会让髋、脊柱、腕部在极小甚至无外力下就骨折。若为夹板固定而尝试拉直患肢时遇到阻力或疼痛加重——骨关节炎老年患者常见——应停止强行拉直，改为原位固定。

points.en: Joints come in three types: fibrous/synarthroses (no motion — skull sutures, distal tibiofibular joint), cartilaginous/amphiarthroses (minimal motion — pubic symphysis, costosternal joints), and synovial/diarthroses (most mobile — enclosed in a joint capsule, lined by synovial membrane that secretes lubricating synovial fluid). A bursa is a fluid-filled cushioning sac near a joint (olecranon, prepatellar) that can swell rapidly with bleeding after acute trauma.
points.zh: 关节分三类：纤维关节（不动——颅缝、远端胫腓关节）、软骨关节（微动——耻骨联合、肋胸关节）、滑膜关节（最灵活——包裹在关节囊内，内衬滑膜分泌润滑用的滑液）。滑囊是关节附近的含液缓冲囊（鹰嘴滑囊、髌前滑囊），急性外伤后可能因出血而迅速肿胀。

points.en: Tendons connect muscle to bone; ligaments connect bone to bone. Cartilage has a very limited blood supply — it gets nutrients only by diffusion — so a cartilage injury heals poorly compared with bone.
points.zh: 肌腱连接肌肉与骨骼；韧带连接骨与骨。软骨的血供极为有限——只能靠扩散获取营养——所以软骨损伤的愈合能力远不如骨骼。

points.en: Skeletal (voluntary/striated) muscle makes up 40-50% of body weight and, because of its high metabolic demand, has a very rich blood supply — which is exactly why it bleeds significantly when injured. A motor unit (one neuron plus the muscle fibres it innervates) fires all-or-nothing; a stronger contraction comes from recruiting more motor units, not making existing ones fire harder.
points.zh: 骨骼肌（随意肌/横纹肌）约占体重的 40%-50%，因代谢需求高而血供丰富——这也是它受伤后出血往往明显的原因。一个运动单位（一条神经元加上它支配的肌纤维）遵循「全有全无」原则收缩；更强的收缩力来自募集更多运动单位，而不是让已激活的单位收缩得更用力。

points.en: Upper-extremity innervation comes from the brachial plexus (spinal roots C5-T1), which resolves into five named nerves: axillary, radial, musculocutaneous, ulnar, median. Lower-extremity innervation comes from the lumbosacral plexus (L1-S4), which forms the femoral nerve and the sciatic nerve — the latter splitting at the popliteal fossa into the peroneal and tibial nerves.
points.zh: 上肢神经支配来自臂丛（脊神经根 C5-T1），分出五条命名神经：腋神经、桡神经、肌皮神经、尺神经、正中神经。下肢神经支配来自腰骶丛（L1-S4），形成股神经和坐骨神经——后者在腘窝分为腓神经和胫神经。

points.en: Upper-extremity arterial supply runs subclavian → axillary → brachial → radial + ulnar → digital arteries. Lower-extremity supply runs external iliac → femoral → popliteal → anterior tibial (→ dorsalis pedis) + posterior tibial → digital arteries of the toes. These are exactly the pulses you're feeling for on every distal CSM check: radial/ulnar in the arm, dorsalis pedis/posterior tibial in the leg.
points.zh: 上肢动脉供血路径：锁骨下动脉→腋动脉→肱动脉→桡动脉+尺动脉→指动脉。下肢：髂外动脉→股动脉→腘动脉→胫前动脉（→足背动脉）+胫后动脉→趾动脉。这正是每次做远端 CSM 检查时要摸的那几条脉搏：上肢摸桡/尺动脉，下肢摸足背/胫后动脉。

points.en: Direct force transfers energy at the point of impact — if it exceeds bone strength, a fracture results, and if the impact is near a joint, a dislocation (with or without an accompanying fracture) can follow. For penetrating trauma, the projectile's SPEED matters far more than its size: a high-velocity round shatters bone and causes extensive soft-tissue damage well beyond the entry point.
points.zh: 直接暴力在撞击点转移能量——若超出骨骼强度即造成骨折，撞击点靠近关节则可能造成脱位（伴或不伴骨折）。穿透伤中，抛射物的速度远比其体积更能决定伤害程度：高速弹丸能粉碎骨骼，造成远超入口范围的大面积软组织损伤。

points.en: Indirect force is applied at one site but the injury shows up somewhere else, as the force travels through the skeleton until it hits a structurally weaker point. Classic example: a knee striking the dashboard in a collision drives force proximally up the femur until it fractures the femoral neck — the knee itself may be uninjured.
points.zh: 间接暴力作用在一处，损伤却出现在另一处——力沿骨骼传导，直到遇上结构相对薄弱的环节。经典例子：车祸中膝盖撞上仪表板，力沿股骨向近端传导，最终使股骨颈骨折——膝盖本身反而可能完好。

points.en: FOOSH (fall on outstretched hand) is the textbook example of force travelling proximally along a chain: scaphoid fracture (direct impact) → Colles fracture of the distal radius/ulna (the 'silver fork' deformity) → elbow fracture-dislocation → shoulder fracture-dislocation → clavicle fracture. Tenderness at any one point means you must screen the whole chain, not just the obvious site.
points.zh: 跌倒手掌撑地（FOOSH）是力沿链条向近端传导的教科书例子：舟状骨骨折（直接撞击）→桡尺骨远端 Colles 骨折（「银叉样」畸形）→肘关节骨折脱位→肩关节骨折脱位→锁骨骨折。链条上任何一点有压痛，都意味着要筛查整条链，而不只是最明显的那一处。

points.en: Twisting injuries (football, skiing) happen when the distal limb is fixed — a cleat or ski boot holding the foot — while torsional force builds proximally, tearing tendons/ligaments and producing spiral fractures. Fatigue (stress) fractures come from repetitive stress rather than a single event; when they occur in a metatarsal after prolonged walking, marching, or dancing they're specifically called march fractures.
points.zh: 扭转伤（足球、滑雪）发生在远端肢体被固定（鞋钉或滑雪靴卡住脚部）而近端扭转力不断增大时，撕裂肌腱韧带并造成螺旋形骨折。疲劳（应力）骨折源自反复应力而非单次事件；发生在跖骨、由长时间行走/行军/跳舞引起的，专门称为行军骨折。

points.en: A pathologic fracture happens when force that wouldn't normally harm healthy bone breaks bone that has been weakened by disease — metastatic cancer, corticosteroid use, or age-related osteoporosis. Suspect it whenever the mechanism seems disproportionately minor for the fracture found.
points.zh: 病理性骨折是指本不足以伤及健康骨骼的外力，作用在因疾病而变脆弱的骨骼上（转移癌、长期使用糖皮质激素、或老年骨质疏松）——当骨折与致伤机制明显不成比例时，都要怀疑这一点。

points.en: Memorize the associated-fracture pairings — finding one should trigger a search for the other: scapular fracture → rib fracture / pulmonary contusion / pneumothorax; scaphoid fracture → wrist, elbow, or shoulder fracture; pelvic fracture → lumbosacral spine and other long-bone fractures, intra-abdominal or genitourinary injury; hip dislocation → acetabulum or femoral-head fracture; femoral fracture → ipsilateral hip dislocation; patellar fracture → ipsilateral hip fracture-dislocation; knee dislocation → tibial fracture, and the distal pulse may be absent; calcaneal fracture (axial load, e.g. a fall landing on the feet) → ankle, leg, hip, pelvis, or lumbar-spine fracture, and check the OTHER calcaneus too.
points.zh: 务必记住这些「伴发骨折」组合——发现其一就要主动排查另一个：肩胛骨骨折→肋骨骨折/肺挫伤/气胸；舟状骨骨折→腕、肘或肩关节骨折；骨盆骨折→腰骶椎和其他长骨骨折、腹腔内或泌尿生殖系统损伤；髋关节脱位→髋臼或股骨头骨折；股骨骨折→同侧髋关节脱位；髌骨骨折→同侧髋关节骨折脱位；膝关节脱位→胫骨骨折，且远端脉搏可能消失；跟骨骨折（轴向负荷，如双脚落地的高处坠落）→踝、小腿、髋、骨盆或腰椎骨折，且要检查对侧跟骨。

points.en: A fracture is a break in bone continuity from force (single or repetitive) that exceeds the bone's strength; that strength is itself modified by age, osteoporosis, nutrition, and disease. By the direction the fracture line travels: linear (parallel to the long axis, low-energy), transverse (straight across at a right angle, direct low-energy blow), oblique (angled across, direct or twisting force), spiral (encircles the bone, twisting injury), impacted (one bone end wedged into another, fall from height), pathologic (erosion or abnormal overgrowth from cancer).
points.zh: 骨折是骨骼连续性中断，源于单次或反复应力超出骨骼强度；骨骼强度本身受年龄、骨质疏松、营养和疾病影响。按骨折线走向分：线性骨折（与长轴平行，低能量）、横行骨折（垂直横断，直接低能量打击）、斜行骨折（斜向横断，直接或扭转力）、螺旋骨折（环绕骨干，扭转伤）、嵌插骨折（一骨端楔入另一骨端，高处坠落）、病理性骨折（癌症导致的骨质侵蚀或异常增生）。

points.en: By fragment count: comminuted (more than 2 fragments in one area, high-energy e.g. crush) vs segmental (more than 2 fragments but in different parts of the same bone, also high-energy). By cortices involved: complete (both cortices break, high-energy) vs incomplete (one cortex, low-energy).
points.zh: 按骨折块数量分：粉碎性骨折（同一区域超过 2 块碎片，高能量如挤压伤）vs 节段性骨折（超过 2 块碎片但分布在同一骨的不同部位，同样高能量）。按累及皮质数分：完全性骨折（两侧皮质都断，高能量）vs 不完全性骨折（仅一侧皮质，低能量）。

points.en: Three fracture patterns occur almost exclusively in children, because their bones are more pliable: greenstick (the convex cortex breaks but the concave cortex stays intact, typically in the proximal metaphysis/diaphysis of the tibia or radius), buckle/torus (compression loading buckles one cortex while the opposite cortex pulls away from the physis — classically the distal radius from a FOOSH), and plastic deformation (numerous micro-fractures on the compressed side bend the bone without a clean break, most often radius/ulna/tibia/fibula/clavicle in children and young adults).
points.zh: 三种骨折型态几乎只见于儿童，因为儿童骨骼更具韧性：青枝骨折（凸侧皮质断裂、凹侧皮质仍完整，典型见于胫骨或桡骨的近端干骺端/骨干）、隆突（torus）骨折（压缩负荷使一侧皮质隆起、对侧皮质从骺板处被拉离——典型是 FOOSH 造成的桡骨远端）、塑性变形（受压侧大量微小骨折使骨骼弯曲而不完全断裂，最常见于儿童和青年的桡尺骨、胫腓骨、锁骨）。

points.en: By displacement: nondisplaced (bone stays aligned despite the break, low-energy) vs displaced (fragment ends move out of position, high-energy); overriding (muscle pulls the distal fragment alongside the proximal one so the limb shortens — only when a fracture is fully displaced with no bone contact); distraction (a powerful tensile force pulls the bone ends apart, e.g. industrial machinery); avulsion (a forceful muscle contraction tears the muscle's bone-insertion site off, from a sudden 'jerking' motion); depression (blunt trauma pushes a flat bone, e.g. the skull, inward). Angulation means the fracture ends form an angle rather than a straight line, in any of the frontal, sagittal, or transverse planes.
points.zh: 按移位分：无移位（骨折但仍对位对线，低能量）vs 移位（骨端偏离原位，高能量）；重叠移位（肌肉牵拉远端骨块与近端重叠导致肢体缩短——仅见于完全移位、骨端无接触的骨折）；分离移位（强大牵张力将骨端拉开，如工业机械绞伤）；撕脱骨折（肌肉猛烈收缩将其在骨上的止点撕下，常因突然「猛拉」动作）；压缩骨折（钝力将扁骨如颅骨向内压陷）。成角是指骨折两端不在一条直线上、形成夹角，可发生在冠状、矢状或横切面的任一方向。

points.en: Open (compound) fracture: a skin break communicates with the fracture site — even a small nearby skin break should raise suspicion. Closed fracture: skin over the site stays intact. Open fractures bleed MORE than closed ones for two reasons — they're usually higher-energy mechanisms with more soft-tissue damage, and a closed fracture's hematoma builds interstitial pressure that tamponades the bleeding (a closed femur fracture can lose over 1 L before tamponade kicks in), whereas an open fracture lets blood escape freely so tamponade doesn't occur.
points.zh: 开放性（复合）骨折：皮肤破损与骨折部位相通——即便附近只有一个小伤口也要怀疑开放性骨折。闭合性骨折：骨折处皮肤完整。开放性骨折比闭合性骨折出血更多，原因有二——通常是更高能量的机制、软组织损伤更重；而且闭合性骨折的血肿会累积组织间压力形成压塞止血（闭合性股骨骨折可在压塞生效前失血超过 1 L），开放性骨折血液则可自由外流，压塞效应不会发生。

points.en: Fracture signs on exam: deformity (the MOST reliable sign — always compare with the uninjured side), shortening (broken ends override each other — classic in femur fractures because the bone no longer opposes the powerful thigh muscles' spasm), swelling and ecchymosis (bleeding and fluid accumulation), guarding/loss of use (sometimes diagnostic by itself — holding the dorsum of one wrist = likely Colles fracture; head tilted toward a 'knocked-down shoulder' = likely clavicle fracture on that side), point tenderness (nearly universal), and crepitus (a grating sensation on palpation — note it if present, but don't deliberately try to elicit it, since that just adds pain for no clinical benefit).
points.zh: 骨折查体体征：畸形（最可靠的体征——务必与健侧对比）、缩短（断端相互重叠——股骨骨折的典型表现，因为骨骼已无法对抗大腿强壮肌肉的痉挛牵拉）、肿胀和瘀斑（出血和液体积聚）、保护性姿势/拒绝活动（有时本身就有诊断意义——一手托着另一手腕背＝很可能是 Colles 骨折；头部歪向「塌陷的肩膀」＝该侧很可能是锁骨骨折）、压痛（几乎普遍存在）、骨擦音（触诊时的摩擦感——如果出现要记录，但不要刻意诱发，那只会徒增疼痛而无临床意义）。

points.en: The ability to still move or use an injured part does NOT rule out a fracture — always perform a full assessment and transport for evaluation regardless. In an open fracture, exposed bone may be obvious, or the wound may look small and innocuous; any skin break near a suspected fracture should raise suspicion even without visible bone, since the fracture end can rupture the skin and then retract back into the soft tissue.
points.zh: 受伤部位仍能活动或使用，并不能排除骨折——务必完成完整评估并送医评估，不能因为「还能动」就自行判断没事。开放性骨折中，外露骨端可能很明显，也可能伤口看着很小、毫不起眼；只要疑似骨折附近有皮肤破损就要怀疑开放性骨折，即使看不到骨头——因为骨折端可能先刺破皮肤、随后又缩回软组织。

sections.titleZh: 脱位、扭伤、拉伤与关节炎

points.en: In a dislocation, a bone is fully displaced from the joint — articular surfaces no longer touch, and at least part of the joint capsule and some ligaments are disrupted; the dislocated bone is then held out of place by muscle spasm. Always suspect an accompanying fracture until radiographs rule it out. A subluxation is a PARTIAL dislocation — articular surfaces stay partly in contact and the patient may retain some joint motion — but left untreated it can still cause persistent joint instability and pain.
points.zh: 脱位是指骨骼完全脱离关节——关节面不再接触，至少部分关节囊和部分韧带已断裂；脱位的骨骼由肌肉痉挛维持在错位状态。在影像学排除之前，都要怀疑合并骨折。半脱位是部分脱位——关节面仍部分接触，病人可能还保留一定活动度——但若不处理，仍可能造成持续的关节不稳和疼痛。

points.en: A diastasis is a widened gap between two structures normally held fixed by ligaments — e.g. pubic symphysis diastasis when the ligaments holding it together are disrupted. A dislocation is urgent because of its potential for neurovascular compromise distal to the injury: nerve compression causes numbness/weakness, artery compression causes absent distal pulses (a classic example is a knee dislocation occluding the popliteal artery) — always check pulse/motor/sensory (PMS) both BEFORE and AFTER splinting.
points.zh: 耻骨联合分离（diastasis）是指两个原本由韧带固定的结构之间间隙变宽——例如耻骨联合的韧带断裂后间隙增大。脱位属于紧急情况，因为它有导致远端神经血管受损的风险：神经受压引起麻木/无力，动脉受压导致远端脉搏消失（经典例子是膝关节脱位压闭腘动脉）——夹板固定前后都必须检查脉搏/运动/感觉（PMS）。

points.en: Sprains (ligament stretched or torn) most often affect the ankle or knee from a sudden twist beyond normal range with a transient subluxation. Unlike fractures and dislocations, sprains usually show no deformity, and mobility is limited by pain rather than joint incongruity — but since it's hard to reliably tell the two apart in the field, treat every severe sprain as a probable fracture. General management uses PRICED (Protect, Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation, consider analgesic Drugs) — the same mnemonic covers strains, Achilles rupture, and tendinitis/bursitis in this chapter too.
points.zh: 扭伤（韧带被拉伸或撕裂）最常见于踝或膝，因关节突然扭转超出正常活动范围并伴短暂半脱位所致。与骨折脱位不同，扭伤通常没有畸形，活动受限是因为疼痛而非关节结构错位——但院前很难可靠区分两者，所以应把每一处严重扭伤都当作疑似骨折处理。通用处理用 PRICED（保护、休息、冰敷、加压、抬高、考虑镇痛药）——本章后面的拉伤、跟腱断裂、腱鞘炎/滑囊炎处理也沿用这同一套口诀。

points.en: A strain (pulled muscle/tendon) results from violent contraction or over-stretching; deformity is usually absent, swelling is minor, passive movement can increase pain, and bruising may take hours to appear as torn fibres bleed under the skin. Achilles tendon rupture typically hits adults over 30 in start-and-stop sports (basketball, football): sudden pain from heel to calf, sudden inability to plantarflex, a palpable defect along the tendon, and a positive Thompson test (prone, squeeze the calf — no plantarflexion of the foot means a likely tear). Recovery from surgery/casting can take up to 6 months.
points.zh: 拉伤（肌肉/肌腱被拉伤）源自剧烈收缩或过度牵拉；通常无畸形、肿胀较轻，被动活动可能加重疼痛，撕裂纤维在皮下出血，瘀斑可能数小时后才显现。跟腱断裂典型见于 30 岁以上、从事急停急转运动（篮球、足球）的成人：突发的足跟到小腿疼痛、突然无法跖屈、沿肌腱可触及凹陷缺损，Thompson 试验阳性（俯卧位挤压小腿——足部不出现跖屈提示很可能已断裂）。手术或多次石膏固定后的恢复期可长达 6 个月。

points.en: Repetitive overuse can inflame a tendon (tendinitis — point tenderness worsened by the causative movement, classically shoulder tendinitis from overhead activity) or a nearby bursa (bursitis — tenderness, swelling, erythema, warmth, worse when the space the bursa occupies gets compressed). Both are managed prehospital with PRICED; many patients ultimately need steroid injections from their physician.
points.zh: 反复过度使用可引起肌腱炎（局部压痛，随致病动作加重，典型是过顶动作引起的肩部肌腱炎）或邻近滑囊炎（压痛、肿胀、发红、发热，滑囊所在空间受挤压时加重）。两者院前均用 PRICED 处理；许多病人最终仍需医生的类固醇注射治疗。

points.en: The three most common types of arthritis: osteoarthritis (wear-and-tear disease of aging joints — pain/stiffness worse with use, crepitus, commonly spine/hands/knees/hips, risk rises with age/obesity/prior joint injury); rheumatoid arthritis (a systemic inflammatory disease that can be mild or fatal — significant bone erosion makes joints more fracture/dislocation-prone, and the CERVICAL SPINE is at particular risk of subluxating with trauma or during intubation); gout (crystal-induced arthritis from hyperuricemia — uric acid crystallizes in a joint, classically the great toe, producing a hot, red, swollen, exquisitely tender joint).
points.zh: 三种最常见的关节炎：骨关节炎（关节随年龄磨损的退行性疾病——疼痛僵硬随活动加重、有摩擦音，常见于脊柱/手/膝/髋，风险随年龄、肥胖、既往关节损伤升高）；类风湿关节炎（一种全身性炎症疾病，可轻可致命——明显的骨侵蚀使关节更易骨折脱位，尤其颈椎在外伤或插管时有较高的半脱位风险）；痛风（高尿酸血症引起的结晶性关节炎——尿酸盐结晶沉积于关节，典型见于大脚趾，表现为关节发热、发红、肿胀、极度压痛）。

sections.titleEn: Injuries That May Signify a Fracture, and Vascular Injuries
sections.titleZh: 提示骨折的其他损伤与血管损伤

points.en: An amputation (partial, with a small tissue bridge still attached, or complete) can hemorrhage severely enough to be life-threatening, and a fracture may coexist with it — always treat the wound and check for an underlying fracture together rather than assuming one explains all the findings.
points.zh: 截肢伤（部分离断、仍有小段组织相连，或完全离断）出血可能严重到危及生命，且可能同时合并骨折——处理伤口的同时要一并排查是否有骨折，不要以为找到一种损伤就够了。

points.en: Open wounds — especially deep lacerations, impaled objects, or penetrating trauma — signal enough energy to have damaged the bone underneath, and some open wounds are actually caused by a fracture end punching through the skin from inside. Whenever the mechanism suggests significant force, keep a high index of suspicion for fracture or deep-structure injury even if the visible wound looks unremarkable.
points.zh: 开放伤——尤其深部裂伤、插入异物或穿透伤——提示能量足以伤及下方骨骼，有些开放伤其实是骨折端从内部顶破皮肤所致。只要受伤机制提示明显外力，即使可见伤口看着不起眼，也要高度怀疑骨折或深部结构损伤。

points.en: Damaged vessels near a musculoskeletal injury can devascularize the body part downstream. The injury patterns to know: contusion of the vessel wall, laceration, kinking/bending, pseudoaneurysm (blood leaking through the wall into a contained cavity), and thrombosis (a clot occludes the vessel when flow slows dramatically). Whatever the mechanism, management is the same: assess and reassess pulses, control bleeding, and maintain intravascular volume with IV fluid.
points.zh: 肌骨损伤附近的血管受损，可能使其下游供血的身体部位失去血供。要认识的损伤型态：血管壁挫伤、撕裂、扭结/折弯、假性动脉瘤（血液经血管壁渗漏进入一个被包裹的腔隙）、血栓形成（血流大幅减慢后被血凝块阻塞）。无论具体机制为何，处理原则一致：评估并反复复评脉搏、控制出血、用静脉补液维持血管内容量。

points.en: Signs of an arterial injury found on palpation of an injured extremity: a pulsatile expanding hematoma, diminished distal pulses compared with the uninjured side, a palpable thrill (vibration synchronized with the heartbeat) over the injury, and bleeding that is difficult to control. Any of these is a serious finding that should prompt rapid transport if it hasn't already begun.
points.zh: 触诊伤肢时提示动脉损伤的体征：搏动性膨大血肿、与健侧对比远端脉搏减弱、伤处可触及与心跳同步的震颤、以及难以控制的出血。出现其中任何一项都是严重表现，若尚未启动快速转运，此时应立即启动。

points.en: Musculoskeletal injuries are almost never an immediate threat to life — a fracture can wait, the airway cannot. Mentally sort every patient into one of four buckets before you commit to a plan: life/limb-threatening condition WITH life/limb-threatening MSK trauma; life-threatening condition with only simple MSK trauma; life/limb-threatening MSK trauma with no other life threats; or an isolated, non-threatening injury.
points.zh: 肌骨损伤几乎从不直接威胁生命——骨折可以等，气道不能等。制定处置计划前，先把病人归入四类之一：危及生命/肢体的情况合并危及生命/肢体的肌骨创伤；危及生命的情况合并单纯的肌骨创伤；危及生命/肢体的肌骨创伤但无其他生命威胁；孤立、不危及生命/肢体的单纯损伤。

points.en: Blood loss adds up fast at each fracture site, and the mL ranges are worth memorizing: a fractured pelvis tops the list at 1,500 to 3,000, a femur follows at 1,000 to 1,500, four sites cluster in the same 250-to-500 band (humerus, tibia/fibula, ankle, and elbow), and the radius or ulna sits lowest of all at 150 to 250. Use these numbers to gauge how aggressive your bleeding-control and resuscitation plan needs to be, keeping volume status, vital signs, and mental status normal while you expedite transport.
points.zh: 各骨折部位的失血量累积得很快，这几组 mL 区间值得背熟：骨盆失血最多，1,500 到 3,000；股骨紧随其后，1,000 到 1,500；肱骨、胫腓骨、踝部、肘部这四处则聚在同一区间，250 到 500；桡骨或尺骨最少，150 到 250。用这些数字判断止血和补液方案该有多积极，目标是在加快转运的同时，把容量状态、生命体征和意识状态维持在正常范围。

points.en: If the initial assessment shows no immediate life threat and only localized MSK trauma, move to a focused history and exam. If the mechanism is significant, complete a rapid trauma assessment on scene and push the detailed physical exam to en route. Your priorities throughout: identify the injuries, prevent further harm to injured structures, support the injured area, and give analgesia when indicated.
points.zh: 如果初步评估未发现即刻生命威胁、只有局限性肌骨创伤，转入针对性病史采集与体检。如果机制显著，现场完成快速创伤评估，把详细体检留到转运途中。全程的优先事项：识别损伤、防止受伤结构进一步受损、支撑伤处、按指征给予镇痛。

points.en: History of present injury: how the incident happened and why, what safety equipment was in use, the patient's position afterward, and a subjective description — did you hear a pop, what's the pain, what can't you do now. Medical history follows SAMPLE and should specifically surface pre-existing MSK conditions and anticoagulant use, since that changes both bleeding risk and analgesia choices.
points.zh: 现病史采集：事件如何发生、为何发生、事发时使用了什么防护装备、事后患者的体位，以及主观描述——有没有听到「啪」的一声、痛不痛、现在有什么功能受限。既往史按 SAMPLE 采集，要特别问出既往肌骨疾病和抗凝药使用情况，这会同时影响出血风险和镇痛药选择。

points.en: Examine with DCAP-BTLS (Deformity, Contusions, Abrasions, Punctures/penetrations, Burns, Tenderness, Lacerations, Swelling) head to toe, and specifically cover the 6 Ps of MUSCULOSKELETAL assessment: Pain, Paralysis, Paraesthesias, Pulselessness, Pallor (or delayed capillary refill in children), and Pressure. Note this is a DIFFERENT six-P list from compartment syndrome's six Ps (Pain/Paraesthesia/Paresis/Pressure/Passive-stretch pain/Pulselessness) — don't mix them up.
points.zh: 用 DCAP-BTLS（畸形、挫伤、擦伤、穿刺/穿透伤、烧伤、压痛、裂伤、肿胀）从头到脚检查，并专门覆盖肌骨评估的 6 个 P：疼痛（Pain）、瘫痪（Paralysis）、感觉异常（Paraesthesias）、无脉（Pulselessness）、苍白（Pallor，儿童表现为毛细血管再充盈延迟）、张力（Pressure）。注意这与筋膜间室综合征的 6 个 P（疼痛/感觉异常/肌力减退/张力增高/被动牵拉痛/无脉）是两套不同的清单，不要混淆。

points.en: Watch for the distracting-injury trap: an obvious open femur fracture can pull the patient's — and your — attention away from a quieter but real injury elsewhere. Distal extremity fractures/dislocations (hands and feet) are the classic ones that get missed this way, so deliberately re-examine beyond the obvious injury.
points.zh: 警惕「分散注意力伤」陷阱：一处明显的开放性股骨骨折会把病人和你的注意力都拉过去，掩盖别处真实存在但没那么显眼的损伤。远端肢体（手和脚）的骨折/脱位最经典地会以这种方式被漏诊，所以要刻意在明显伤之外再做检查。

points.en: For pain assessment use OPQRST — Onset, Provoking/Palliating factors, Quality, Region (plus radiation/referral), Severity (1-10 or a picture scale), Time/duration and trajectory. On inspection, always examine the joint above AND below the injury site, since the injuring force may have affected them too; look for deformity (asymmetry/angulation/shortening/rotation), skin changes, swelling, muscle spasm, abnormal positioning, range-of-motion changes, colour changes, and bleeding.
points.zh: 疼痛评估用 OPQRST——诱因（Onset）、加重/缓解因素（Provoking/Palliating）、性质（Quality）、部位（Region，含放射/牵涉痛）、严重程度（Severity，1-10 分或图示量表）、时间/病程（Time，含变化趋势）。视诊时务必检查伤处的上一关节和下一关节，因为致伤力可能同时波及它们；要看畸形（不对称/成角/缩短/旋转）、皮肤改变、肿胀、肌肉痉挛、异常体位、活动度改变、颜色改变、出血。

points.en: Palpate the injury site plus the regions above and below, identifying point tenderness (note: 'pain' is what the patient feels without touch, 'tenderness' is what palpation elicits — the distinction matters for documentation). Point tenderness is one of the best injury indicators, but it can be absent in intoxicated patients or those with a spinal cord injury, so its absence doesn't clear the area. Compare pulse strength between the injured and uninjured limb every time.
points.zh: 触诊伤处以及上下相邻区域，识别压痛点（注意：「疼痛」是病人未被触碰时的主观感受，「压痛」是触诊时诱发的体征——记录时要分清）。压痛点是最好的损伤指征之一，但在醉酒或脊髓损伤病人身上可能缺失，所以压痛阴性不能排除损伤。每次都要把伤肢和健肢的脉搏强度对比检查。

points.en: Skill Drill 28-1 motor/sensory exam by nerve — know which movement or touch site tests which nerve: elbow flexion (musculocutaneous), elbow extension (radial), thumbs-up (distal radial), 'OK' sign (median), finger spread (ulnar), knee extension (femoral), plantarflexion (tibial), dorsiflexion (deep peroneal); sensory: lateral shoulder/deltoid (axillary), anterolateral forearm (musculocutaneous), thumb web space dorsum (radial), volar thumb/index/middle finger (median), volar small finger (ulnar), anteromedial thigh (femoral), plantar toes (tibial), web space between first/second toes (peroneal).
points.zh: Skill Drill 28-1 按神经做运动/感觉检查——记清哪个动作或触诊部位对应哪条神经：屈肘（肌皮神经）、伸肘（桡神经）、竖大拇指（桡神经远端支）、比「OK」手势（正中神经）、张开手指（尺神经）、伸膝（股神经）、跖屈（胫神经）、背屈（腓深神经）；感觉：肩外侧/三角肌区（腋神经）、前臂前外侧（肌皮神经）、拇指虎口背侧（桡神经）、拇指/食指/中指掌侧（正中神经）、小指掌侧（尺神经）、大腿前内侧（股神经）、足底趾部（胫神经）、第一二趾间蹼（腓神经）。

points.en: When testing motor function, test with AND without resistance (some patients are too weak to overcome any resistance) and test both sides simultaneously for comparison. When testing sensation, ask about spontaneous abnormal sensations first, then do a gross exam by touching both sides at once and asking if they feel the same; severe pain from light touch (hyperalgesia) can be a sign of spinal cord damage. Always document the neurovascular exam even when it's normal, and document any specific deficit found (e.g. 'unable to extend the thumb or wrist').
points.zh: 测试运动功能时要分别测有阻力和无阻力两种情况（有些病人虚弱到无法对抗任何阻力），并同时测双侧以便对比。测试感觉时先问有无自发的异常感觉，再做粗略检查——同时触碰双侧、询问是否感觉一致；轻触即引发剧痛（痛觉过敏）可能提示脊髓损伤。神经血管检查即使结果正常也要记录，发现具体缺损时要写明（如「无法伸展拇指或腕部」）。

sections.titleEn: Pain Control, Cold/Heat Application, and Splinting Principles
sections.titleZh: 镇痛、冷热敷与固定原则

points.en: The prehospital pain-control goal is a tolerable level, not zero pain. Get a baseline severity score first so you have something to measure your interventions against. Simple, always-available measures: splint in anatomic position, rest and elevate the injured part, apply ice or heat as appropriate. When those aren't enough, consider an analgesic — but reserve drugs for hemodynamically stable patients with an isolated MSK injury, get vitals before and after, watch respiratory status, and reassess pain afterward to confirm relief was adequate.
points.zh: 院前镇痛的目标是把疼痛降到可耐受的水平，不是降到零。先取一个基线疼痛评分，这样才有依据评估后续处置的效果。随手可用的简单措施：以解剖位固定、休息抬高患肢、按情况冷敷或热敷。这些不够时再考虑镇痛药——但用药人群限于血流动力学稳定、单纯肌骨损伤的病人，用药前后都要测生命体征，留意呼吸状态，用药后复评疼痛以确认缓解是否充分。

points.en: Anti-inflammatory analgesics work because the body's own inflammatory mediators cause pain — temporarily interrupting that process relieves it. Giving analgesia BEFORE splinting, when time allows, lets the limb tolerate being held in the correct position long enough for the splint to go on properly — remember, holding an injured limb straight for splinting hurts.
points.zh: 抗炎类镇痛药之所以有效，是因为身体自身的炎症介质本身就会致痛——暂时打断这个过程就能缓解疼痛。时间允许时，在夹板固定前先给镇痛药，能让患肢多撑一会儿被摆在正确位置，从而让夹板固定得更到位——毕竟把伤肢摆直等待固定这件事本身就很痛。

points.en: Cold packs are most useful in the first 48 hours after injury — vasoconstriction plus reduced release of inflammatory mediators cuts both pain and swelling. Heat should be AVOIDED in the first 48-72 hours (it can increase pain and swelling during the acute phase); it becomes useful only later, once damaged vessels have clotted, to increase blood flow and ease stiffness — relevant for a patient reporting an injury from several days ago.
points.zh: 冰敷在伤后 48 小时内最有效——血管收缩加上炎症介质释放减少，能同时减轻疼痛和肿胀。伤后 48-72 小时内应避免热敷（急性期热敷可能加重疼痛和肿胀）；只有在损伤血管已经凝血之后，热敷才有用——促进局部血流、缓解僵硬，适用于报告受伤已过去数天的病人。

points.en: Splinting supports and prevents motion of the bone ends AND the two adjacent joints. Done correctly it reduces pain, cuts the risk of further damage to nerves/vessels/skin, and helps control bleeding by letting clots form undisturbed where vessels were torn. When a patient with multiple orthopedic injuries needs urgent transport, don't splint each fracture one by one — immobilize as best you can and prioritize getting to definitive care.
points.zh: 夹板固定的作用是支撑骨折端并同时限制其上下两个相邻关节的活动。正确固定能减轻疼痛、降低神经/血管/皮肤进一步损伤的风险，还能让已撕裂血管处的血凝块不受干扰地形成，从而帮助控制出血。多发骨科损伤且需紧急转运的病人，不要逐一给每处骨折上夹板——尽力做到最基本的固定，优先送达确定性治疗。

points.en: Splinting checklist: fully expose and visualize the area first; record distal PMS before AND after splinting; cover any wound with a dry sterile dressing before splinting (brush away surface debris around an open fracture, but never probe the wound or push exposed bone ends back under the skin — that just adds contamination); don't move the patient before splinting unless there's an immediate hazard; pad generously to prevent local pressure; support the site manually (one hand above, one below) until the splint is secured; splint firmly but never so tight it occludes circulation; leave fingers/toes exposed when possible to keep monitoring colour, temperature, and condition; if feasible, apply cold and elevate the splinted limb afterward.
points.zh: 夹板固定检查清单：先充分暴露患处以便观察；固定前后都要记录远端 PMS；固定前用干燥无菌敷料覆盖伤口（刷去开放性骨折周围表面的碎屑，但绝不能探查伤口或把外露骨端推回皮下——这只会增加污染）；除非有即刻危险，否则固定前不要移动病人；充分加衬垫以防局部受压；固定完成前用一手在上、一手在下徒手支撑伤处；固定要牢固但绝不能压闭远端循环；条件允许应露出手指/脚趾以便持续监测颜色、温度、状态；条件允许，固定后冰敷并抬高患肢。

points.en: For a severely angulated long-bone fracture, gentle longitudinal traction with a smooth firm grip (no sudden jerky movements) can realign it toward a more natural position and improve circulation. But do NOT attempt to straighten a fracture that involves a JOINT without medical direction first — the pain of forcing an unstable joint straight usually outweighs the benefit, UNLESS distal circulation is already lost, in which case repositioning becomes worth attempting. If the patient reports severe pain or resists movement, stop traction, splint in the position of deformity, and monitor distal PMS closely instead.
points.zh: 严重成角的长骨骨折，可用平稳有力（无突然猛拉）的手法施加轻柔纵向牵引，使其更接近自然对位并改善循环。但涉及关节的骨折，未经医疗指导授权不要尝试拉直——强行拉直不稳定关节所带来的疼痛通常超过其益处，除非远端循环已经丧失，此时才值得尝试复位。若病人反映剧痛或抗拒活动，应停止牵引，改为在畸形位固定，并密切监测远端 PMS。

sections.titleEn: Splint Types, Sling/Swath, and Traction Splints
sections.titleZh: 夹板种类、悬吊带与牵引夹板

points.en: Rigid splints (padded board, cardboard, aluminum ladder/SAM splint) must be padded generously for even pressure and long enough to secure well above and below the fracture — past the adjacent joints. Wrap firmly enough to hold the splint in place but never so tight it occludes circulation, and leave fingers/toes exposed so distal circulation stays visible.
points.zh: 硬质夹板（衬垫木板、硬纸板、铝制梯形/SAM 夹板）必须充分加衬垫以均匀分散压力，长度要足以固定到骨折上下方——超过相邻的两个关节。缠绕要牢固到能固定住夹板，但绝不能压闭远端循环，并露出手指/脚趾以便持续观察远端血供。

points.en: A triangular-bandage sling holds the injured arm against the chest, taking weight off the shoulder/arm — secure it so the hand sits slightly higher than the elbow and fingers stay visible for circulation checks. A narrower-folded version for a suspected HUMERUS fracture supports just the forearm/wrist, letting gravity itself pull gentle traction toward a more anatomic position. A swath (one or more triangular bandages binding the arm to the chest wall) adds stability — especially useful for clavicle injuries and anterior shoulder dislocations — but must not be so tight it restricts chest expansion, and should not be used with a suspected neck injury.
points.zh: 三角巾悬吊带把伤臂固定在胸前，减轻肩/臂的承重——要让手部略高于肘部，并露出手指以便检查循环。针对疑似肱骨骨折的窄折叠版仅支撑前臂和腕部，利用重力本身对骨折产生轻柔的牵引、帮助恢复解剖对位。加一条或多条三角巾把手臂缚定在胸壁上形成的悬吊-固定带组合（swath），能进一步增加稳定性——尤其适用于锁骨损伤和肩关节前脱位——但不能绑得影响胸廓扩张，且怀疑颈部损伤时不应使用。

points.en: Pneumatic (air) splints suit lower-leg or forearm fractures and, by applying pressure, help slow small-vessel bleeding and limit swelling — but they are NOT for angulated fractures or fractures involving a joint (they forcefully try to straighten it) and NOT for open fractures with exposed bone. Inflate only until finger pressure makes a slight dent; never use a compressed-air tank. Watch for overinflation if the patient moves from cold to warm (trapped air expands) or gains altitude on an unpressurized air ambulance — either can raise pressure enough to stop pulses.
points.zh: 气动（空气）夹板适用于小腿或前臂骨折，靠施加压力帮助减缓小血管出血、限制肿胀——但不适用于成角骨折或累及关节的骨折（会强行把它们拉直），也不适用于骨端外露的开放性骨折。充气以手指按压能压出一个轻微凹陷为度；绝不能用压缩空气罐充气。病人从寒冷环境进入温暖环境（囊内空气受热膨胀）或乘坐未增压的空中救护车升高海拔时都要警惕过度充气——两者都可能使压力升高到压闭脉搏的程度。

points.en: Vacuum splints use a sealed bag of small plastic beads; a suction pump evacuates the air so the beads lock together into a rigid, custom-moulded shape — a mattress-sized version can immobilize the whole patient and is a good option for an older patient with abnormal spinal curvature, though it's bulky and needs a suction pump to work.
points.zh: 真空夹板是一个密封的塑料小珠袋；抽气泵抽出内部空气后，小珠相互锁紧形成贴合肢体的坚硬定型——床垫大小的版本可固定整个病人，对脊柱有异常弯曲的老年病人是不错的选择，但体积较大且需要配备抽气泵才能使用。

points.en: A femur fracture lets the powerful thigh muscles spasm unopposed, pulling the broken ends to override each other — the thigh shortens and its shape changes from a cylinder toward a sphere, and a sphere holds substantially more blood volume than a cylinder of the same limb. A traction splint provides constant counter-pull that prevents that overriding, maintains alignment, reduces pain, AND cuts blood loss by keeping the thigh's shape closer to its normal cylindrical form.
points.zh: 股骨骨折发生后，强壮的大腿肌肉不受对抗地痉挛，把断端相互拉拽重叠——大腿因此缩短，形状从圆柱体趋向球体，而同样大小的球体能容纳的血量远大于圆柱体。牵引夹板提供持续的反向牵引力，阻止断端重叠、维持对位、减轻疼痛，同时因为让大腿形状更接近正常的圆柱形而减少失血量。

points.en: Traction splints (Sager and Hare are the common devices) are indicated ONLY for suspected mid-shaft femur fractures — they are contraindicated with an additional fracture at or below the knee on the same limb, and contraindicated with a suspected pelvic fracture. Application sequence: assess distal PMS first; one provider manually stabilizes the leg and applies traction while the partner preps and positions the splint alongside the uninjured leg to size it; secure the thigh/ischial and ankle straps; apply gentle longitudinal traction to realign the limb; add the leg-support straps; recheck that the thigh/ischial and ankle straps are still secure; reassess PMS before moving to transport.
points.zh: 牵引夹板（常用 Sager 和 Hare 两种装置）仅用于疑似股骨干骨折——同侧肢体在膝或膝以下另有骨折时禁用，疑似骨盆骨折时也禁用。上夹板顺序：先评估远端 PMS；一人徒手固定患肢并施加牵引，同时搭档取健侧腿比量确定夹板长度并做好准备；固定大腿/坐骨带和踝部吊带；施加轻柔纵向牵引使肢体复位对线；加上腿部支撑带；再次确认大腿/坐骨带和踝部吊带仍然牢固；转运前复评 PMS。

points.en: Buddy splinting immobilizes an injured finger or toe by taping it to an adjacent uninjured digit, with a gauze pad placed between the two digits and tape kept off the joints — snug enough to hold, never tight enough to cut off circulation.
points.zh: 并指固定用胶带把受伤的手指或脚趾绑在相邻健康的指/趾上，两指间垫一块纱布，胶带避开关节——固定要牢但绝不能勒到影响循环。

points.en: Don't fixate on the injured extremity and forget there's a whole patient attached to it — complication risk tracks the force involved, the injury's location, and the patient's overall health, and any MSK injury is likely accompanied by bleeding proportional to the force that caused it.
points.zh: 不要只盯着受伤的肢体而忘了肢体连着一整个人——并发症风险取决于致伤力大小、损伤部位和病人整体健康状况，而任何肌骨损伤都可能伴随与致伤力大小成正比的出血。

points.en: Open-fracture infection can progress from local wound infection to deep bone infection (osteomyelitis) to systemic infection and death. Prevention is field-level: irrigate generously with sterile saline/water to remove surface debris around the wound, but never enter or probe the fracture site itself trying to retrieve debris — that just drives contamination deeper.
points.zh: 开放性骨折感染可能从局部伤口感染发展为深部骨感染（骨髓炎），再到全身性感染乃至死亡。预防措施在院前就要做到位：用无菌生理盐水/清水大量冲洗伤口周围的表面碎屑，但绝不能为了取出碎屑而探查骨折部位本身——那只会把污染推得更深。

points.en: Neurovascular structures are normally shielded deep within a limb by the skeleton itself — for example the brachial plexus sits protected within the axilla by the shoulder girdle. A fracture of the shoulder girdle or proximal humerus can displace fragments that lacerate or impale the plexus, and a joint dislocation is a particularly high-risk mechanism because nerves/vessels near a joint are more tightly tethered to soft tissue and less able to simply move out of the way — knee dislocation is the classic example.
points.zh: 神经血管结构平时深藏在骨骼保护之下——例如臂丛神经就藏在肩带保护的腋窝深处。肩带或肱骨近端骨折移位的碎片可能撕裂或刺穿臂丛；关节脱位是尤其高风险的机制，因为关节附近的神经血管被更紧密地固定在软组织上、难以像别处一样「让开」——膝关节脱位就是经典例子。

points.en: Compartment syndrome can complicate a fracture, dislocation, crush injury, vascular injury, or severe soft-tissue injury — and a common misconception is that OPEN fractures are somehow safe from it; they are not. Field management stays simple: elevate the extremity to heart level (never above), apply cold packs, loosen constrictive clothing/splint material, and transport on an emergency basis — there is no field fix, only surgery. (For the full six-Ps picture and the 6-hour irreversibility threshold, see Chapter 22.)
points.zh: 筋膜间室综合征可继发于骨折、脱位、挤压伤、血管损伤或严重软组织损伤——一个常见误区是以为开放性骨折不会发生间室综合征，这是错的。院前处置很简单：把患肢抬高至心脏水平（绝不高于心脏）、冰敷、松开过紧的衣物或夹板材料，并按急症转运——院前没有根治手段，唯一的确定性治疗是手术。（完整的六个 P 表现和 6 小时不可逆阈值见第 22 章。）

points.en: Thromboembolic disease (DVT/pulmonary embolism) is a significant cause of death after MSK injury, especially pelvic or lower-extremity injuries that lead to prolonged immobilization. DVT signs: disproportionate limb swelling, discomfort that worsens with use, warmth and erythema. A dislodged clot causing PE presents with sudden dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, syncope, tachypnea, tachycardia, low-grade fever, right-heart failure, shock, or even cardiac arrest.
points.zh: 血栓栓塞性疾病（深静脉血栓/肺栓塞）是肌骨损伤后死亡的重要原因，尤其是导致长期制动的骨盆或下肢损伤。深静脉血栓体征：与其他部位不成比例的肢体肿胀、活动后加重的不适感、局部发热发红。血栓脱落引起肺栓塞时表现为突发呼吸困难、胸膜炎性胸痛、晕厥、呼吸急促、心动过速、低热、右心衰竭、休克，甚至心搏骤停。

points.en: Fat embolism syndrome is a separate risk specific to long-bone or pelvic fractures: fat droplets from bone marrow enter circulation and lodge in the lungs, brain, or skin, typically producing symptoms 12-72 hours after injury. Pulmonary involvement mimics a PE; other-organ involvement can show altered LOC (agitation to coma), skin petechiae, or fever. Prehospital treatment for either thromboembolic disease or fat embolism is the same and limited: airway, oxygenation, intravascular volume, and rapid transport — avoid large-volume boluses in suspected massive PE, since they can shift the interventricular septum and worsen shock.
points.zh: 脂肪栓塞综合征是长骨或骨盆骨折特有的另一种风险：骨髓中的脂肪滴进入循环并栓塞在肺、脑或皮肤，典型在伤后 12-72 小时出现症状。累及肺部时表现类似肺栓塞；累及其他器官时可见意识改变（从躁动到昏迷）、皮肤瘀点或发热。无论是血栓栓塞还是脂肪栓塞，院前治疗都同样有限：维持气道、供氧、维持血管内容量、快速转运——疑似大面积肺栓塞时避免大量补液，因为可能推移室间隔、加重休克。

points.en: Long-term disability is one of the most devastating MSK outcomes — even a successfully repaired limb often means extensive rehabilitation or chronic pain that keeps a patient off work for a long time. Careful field evaluation and management directly mitigates this risk: reducing infection risk, identifying threats to the limb, minimizing pain, and getting the patient to the right facility all shrink the eventual disability window.
points.zh: 长期残疾是肌骨损伤最严重的后果之一——即便肢体修复成功，也常意味着漫长的康复期或慢性疼痛，让病人长时间无法工作。院前的细致评估和处置能直接降低这一风险：减少感染机会、识别威胁肢体的因素、最大限度减轻疼痛、送到合适的医疗机构，这些都能缩短最终的失能期。

sections.titleEn: Specific Fractures: Shoulder Girdle and Upper Extremity

points.en: Clavicle fractures are common, especially in children, usually at the middle third from a FOOSH or direct lateral trauma to the shoulder (contact sports, snowboarding, cycling) — expect shoulder pain, swelling, reluctance to raise the arm, and the head tilted toward the injured side. Shoulder fractures (glenoid fossa, humeral head, humeral neck) more often affect older patients from a FOOSH (younger patients tend to dislocate rather than fracture, since their bone is stronger); deformity is often subtle, but swelling/ecchymosis/pain with movement is prominent, and a brachial plexus injury can accompany it.
points.zh: 锁骨骨折很常见，尤其在儿童，多发生在锁骨中段，机制是跌倒手撑地或肩部直接受到侧向外力（接触性运动、单板滑雪、骑行）——表现为肩部疼痛、肿胀、不愿抬臂、头部歪向伤侧。肩部骨折（关节盂、肱骨头、肱骨颈）更多见于跌倒手撑地的老年患者（年轻人骨质更强，同样的外力更容易导致脱位而非骨折）；畸形往往不明显，但活动时肿胀/瘀斑/疼痛突出，还可能合并臂丛神经损伤。

points.en: The scapula is well-protected, so a fracture here means violent direct trauma — always screen for associated intrathoracic injury (pneumothorax, hemothorax, rib fractures), axillary artery/nerve injury, and brachial plexus injury. Shoulder-girdle fractures are generally treated with sling and swath holding the arm against the chest in a position of comfort; given the force required for a scapular fracture, spinal precautions are usually warranted too.
points.zh: 肩胛骨受保护良好，一旦骨折意味着遭受了猛烈的直接暴力——务必筛查伴发的胸腔内损伤（气胸、血胸、肋骨骨折）、腋动脉/神经损伤和臂丛神经损伤。肩带骨折通常用悬吊带加固定带、将手臂固定在舒适位贴向胸壁；考虑到造成肩胛骨骨折所需的力度，通常也需要采取脊柱防护措施。

points.en: Midshaft humerus fractures usually follow high-energy trauma in younger patients and show substantial deformity, swelling, ecchymosis, gross instability, and crepitus. Watch specifically for the RADIAL NERVE — it runs in a bony groove along the humerus and can be entrapped at the fracture site; the classic sign is wrist drop (unable to extend the wrist and fingers). If angulated, gentle longitudinal traction may correct it (stop if pain is severe or neurovascular status worsens); splint from axilla to elbow, then add sling and swath, then cold packs.
points.zh: 肱骨干骨折多见于年轻患者的高能量外伤，表现为明显畸形、肿胀、瘀斑、明显不稳和骨擦音。要特别留意桡神经——它沿肱骨骨沟走行，可能在骨折处被卡压；典型表现是垂腕（无法伸腕伸指）。若有成角，可用轻柔纵向牵引纠正（若疼痛剧烈或神经血管状态恶化则停止）；用夹板从腋窝固定到肘部，再加悬吊带和固定带，最后冰敷。

points.en: Supracondylar humerus fractures are the classic pediatric elbow injury (FOOSH with the elbow extended): the distal fragment is pushed posterior while the shaft is pulled anterior, compressing the brachial artery and the radial/median nerves. Brachial artery compromise risks compartment syndrome of the forearm progressing to Volkmann ischemic contracture — a clawlike, nonfunctional hand from degenerated forearm flexor muscles. Radial head fractures (FOOSH or direct blow) carry similar nerve/vessel risk and need the same careful neurovascular exam.
points.zh: 肱骨髁上骨折是儿童肘部损伤的典型代表（肘伸直位跌倒手撑地）：远端骨块被推向后方，肱骨干则被拉向前方，压迫肱动脉和桡/正中神经。肱动脉受累有引发前臂筋膜间室综合征的风险，进而发展为 Volkmann 缺血性挛缩——前臂屈肌变性导致的爪形、无功能手。桡骨头骨折（跌倒手撑地或直接打击）同样有神经血管损伤风险，需要同样细致的神经血管检查。

points.en: Elbow-region fracture treatment is the same regardless of exact location: repeatedly reassess for compartment syndrome, document a neurovascular exam BEFORE splinting, splint in the position found if the distal pulse is strong (apply cold packs), and consult medical control about attempting reduction only if the distal pulse is absent or there's a neurologic deficit — either way, transport urgently to definitive care.
points.zh: 无论具体部位，肘部骨折的处置原则一致：反复评估是否出现筋膜间室综合征，固定前先记录神经血管检查结果，若远端脉搏有力则原位固定（并冰敷），只有当远端脉搏消失或有神经功能缺损时才考虑咨询医疗指导是否尝试复位——无论哪种情况都要紧急转运至确定性治疗。

points.en: Forearm fractures may involve the radius, ulna, or (most commonly) both, from a direct blow (nightstick fracture of the ulna) or a FOOSH (Colles fracture — a distal radius fracture in older, often osteoporotic patients, producing the classic dorsally-angulated 'silver fork' deformity). Splint the entire forearm including wrist and elbow, apply cold packs, and reassess frequently for compartment syndrome AND acute carpal tunnel syndrome (median nerve compression → pain/paraesthesia in the palmar thumb, index, and middle fingers).
points.zh: 前臂骨折可累及桡骨、尺骨，或（更常见）两者同时受累，机制是直接打击（尺骨的「警棍骨折」）或跌倒手撑地（Colles 骨折——多见于骨质疏松老年患者的桡骨远端骨折，形成典型的背侧成角「银叉样」畸形）。固定要覆盖整个前臂含腕部和肘部，冰敷，并反复评估是否出现筋膜间室综合征和急性腕管综合征（正中神经受压→拇指、食指、中指掌侧疼痛麻木）。

points.en: Scaphoid fracture: tenderness in the anatomic snuffbox (the hollow at the base of the thumb between its tendons when thumbs-up) after a FOOSH — its major complications are avascular necrosis and poor healing because the bone's blood supply is limited and precarious. Boxer's fracture: neck of the 5th metacarpal, from punching a hard object. A 'fight bite' — knuckle struck a mouth — is a special open wound: irrigate copiously, check if a tooth fragment could be embedded (a foreign body needing removal), and flag the human-mouth infection risk to the receiving hospital.
points.zh: 舟状骨骨折：跌倒手撑地后，在解剖鼻烟壶区（竖起拇指时其两条肌腱之间的凹陷）出现压痛——主要并发症是缺血性坏死和愈合不良，因为该骨血供有限且极不稳定。拳击手骨折：第五掌骨颈骨折，常因击打硬物所致。「打架咬伤」（拳头击中对方嘴部）是特殊的开放伤——需大量冲洗，检查是否有牙齿碎片嵌入（属于需取出的异物），并向接收医院明确提示人类口腔带来的感染风险。

points.en: Metacarpal shaft fractures (crush or direct trauma) can show abnormal finger rotation/alignment and palm swelling — check hand/finger neurovascular status carefully, since compartment syndrome can develop within the hand after a crush mechanism. Mallet finger (baseball fracture): a finger jammed by a ball avulses the extensor tendon's insertion, and the patient cannot extend the distal phalanx, which stays flexed.
points.zh: 掌骨干骨折（挤压或直接外伤）可见手指旋转/对位异常和手掌肿胀——要仔细检查手/手指的神经血管状态，因为挤压机制后手部也可能出现筋膜间室综合征。锤状指（棒球指）：手指被球猛烈顶撞，撕脱伸肌腱在末节指骨的止点，导致病人无法伸直远节指骨、维持在屈曲位。

points.en: Wrist/hand fracture treatment: splint in the position of function — wrist in about 30° of extension with fingers slightly flexed (a 5-8 cm gauze roll in the palm achieves this) — secured to a rigid splint extending to the elbow and slightly elevated to limit swelling. For isolated digit injuries, a padded flexible splint or buddy taping works well. Ask (and pass along to the hospital) whether the patient is left- or right-handed, since hand injuries carry outsized long-term disability risk for people who rely on their hands for work.
points.zh: 腕/手骨折的固定原则：以功能位固定——腕关节背伸约 30°、手指略屈曲（掌心放一卷 5-8 cm 直径的纱布即可实现），再固定到延伸至肘部、略抬高以减少肿胀的硬质夹板上。孤立性手指损伤可用软衬垫可弯曲夹板或并指固定。要询问（并转告医院）病人是左利手还是右利手，因为手部损伤对靠手吃饭的病人来说，长期致残风险格外突出。

sections.titleEn: Specific Fractures: Pelvis and Lower Extremity

points.en: Pelvic fractures are under 3% of all fractures but are disproportionately deadly: mortality runs 8-50% depending on severity, exceeding 50% when the fracture is open or has an associated vascular injury. Death is usually from massive hemorrhage — the vessels most often damaged are pelvic VEINS, though the internal/external iliac arteries and lumbar vessels can be involved too; structures at risk include the bladder, urethra, rectum, vagina, and sacral nerve plexus, plus the lumbar/sacral nerves and the sciatic and femoral nerves.
points.zh: 骨盆骨折占全部骨折不到 3%，但致死率明显不成比例：死亡率随严重程度在 8%-50% 之间，若骨折开放或合并血管损伤，死亡率可超过 50%。死因通常是大出血——最常受损的是骨盆内的静脉，但髂内/髂外动脉和腰部血管也可能受累；有风险的结构包括膀胱、尿道、直肠、阴道和骶神经丛，以及腰骶神经、坐骨神经和股神经。

points.en: Three high-energy pelvic-ring patterns: lateral compression (side impact — the struck side rotates internally around the sacrum, pelvic VOLUME DECREASES, less often massively hemorrhagic but frequently comes with injuries elsewhere); anterior-posterior compression / 'open-book' (head-on MVC, motorcycle collision, or a pedestrian struck head-on — the pubic symphysis and posterior ligaments tear apart, pelvic volume INCREASES greatly, and massive blood loss potential follows); vertical shear (a fall landing on the feet drives force up through the legs, displacing one or both sides of the pelvis toward the head — anterior component is a rami fracture or symphysis disruption, posterior component is an ilium/sacrum fracture or SI-joint disruption — expect significant limb shortening and a high hemorrhage risk).
points.zh: 三种高能量骨盆环损伤型态：侧方挤压伤（侧面撞击——受撞侧绕骶骨内旋，骨盆容积缩小，大出血相对少见但常合并其他部位损伤）；前后挤压/「开书样」骨折（正面车祸、摩托车事故或行人被正面撞击——耻骨联合和后方韧带被撕裂，骨盆容积大幅增加，大出血风险随之升高）；垂直剪切伤（高处坠落双脚着地，力沿双腿向上传导，使骨盆一侧或双侧向头端移位——前方为耻骨支骨折或耻骨联合分离，后方为髂骨/骶骨骨折或骶髂关节分离——常见明显肢体缩短，出血风险高）。

points.en: Two rarer patterns: a straddle fracture (perineal impact fractures both superior and inferior rami bilaterally — doesn't interfere with weight-bearing, but carries genitourinary complication risk) and an open pelvic fracture (skin, vaginal, or rectal laceration communicating with the fracture — uncommon, from high-velocity mechanisms, and life-threatening).
points.zh: 另外两种较少见的型态：跨骑式骨折（会阴部受撞击导致双侧上下耻骨支骨折——不影响负重，但泌尿生殖系统并发症风险高）以及开放性骨盆骨折（皮肤、阴道或直肠裂伤与骨折相通——少见，源自高速机制，危及生命）。

points.en: Assessing pelvic stability: apply MEDIALLY directed pressure on the iliac wings. The book also describes distracting the pelvis (pushing down and out), but flags that this carries real risk in the uncontrolled prehospital setting — weigh it carefully. A lack of instability on compression does NOT rule out injury, and once instability IS identified, do not re-test it — every additional manipulation raises bleeding risk.
points.zh: 评估骨盆稳定性时，向髂翼施加内向（向中线）压力。教材也提到「牵张」骨盆的手法（向下向外推），但特别提醒这在不受控的院前环境中风险不小——要仔细权衡是否使用。挤压时未引出不稳定并不能排除损伤；而一旦已确认骨盆不稳定，就不要再重复测试——每一次额外操作都会增加出血风险。

points.en: Pelvic fracture treatment: standard trauma ABCs and spinal precautions, IV access with at least one (ideally two) large-bore cannulas, and stabilization by binder or sheet to reduce pelvic volume and tamponade the bleeding vessels — bleeding into the pelvic cavity can exceed 3 L. Once packaged, transport rapidly to a trauma centre and run crystalloid IV to maintain perfusion while avoiding hypertension.
points.zh: 骨盆骨折处置：标准创伤 ABC 和脊柱防护，建立至少一条（最好两条）大口径静脉通路，用固定带或床单缩小骨盆容积、对已出血血管形成压塞——出血进入盆腔可超过 3 升。完成打包后快速转运至创伤中心，静脉输注晶体液维持灌注，同时避免血压过高。

points.en: A hip fracture (femoral head, neck, intertrochanteric, or proximal shaft) is essentially impossible to sub-classify without imaging, so field management is the same regardless of exact site. Femoral neck/intertrochanteric fractures classically follow a fall in an older, osteoporotic patient, but can occur in younger patients from high-energy trauma. A DISPLACED fracture classically shows an externally rotated, shortened leg; a nondisplaced one may look completely normal. Support the limb in the position found (pillows/blankets) — a scoop stretcher is an excellent extrication tool — and manage as any trauma patient: vascular access, analgesia, spinal-precaution consideration, shock monitoring.
points.zh: 髋部骨折（股骨头、颈、转子间或近端骨干）没有影像学几乎无法细分部位，所以院前处置不因具体位置而异。股骨颈/转子间骨折典型见于骨质疏松老年人跌倒后，但年轻人也可能因高能量外伤发生。移位骨折典型表现为患肢外旋并缩短；无移位骨折外观可能完全正常。用枕头/毛毯在原位支撑患肢——铲式担架是极好的搬运工具——其余按标准创伤病人处置：建立静脉通路、镇痛、考虑脊柱防护、监测休克。

points.en: Femoral shaft fractures follow high-energy impact, so their presence should raise suspicion for other injuries too. Expect severe pain, possible severe angulation with significant shortening, or an open wound; exam often shows marked thigh edema, bruising, crepitus, and muscle spasm, with roughly 500-1,500 mL of blood loss possible at the fracture site alone, plus a real risk of fat emboli. Management: shock monitoring, spinal-precaution consideration, vascular access, pain medication, and a TRACTION SPLINT — which reduces both pain and the compartment's volume, minimizing further blood loss.
points.zh: 股骨干骨折源自高能量撞击，其存在本身就应提高对其他损伤的警惕。预期表现为剧痛、可能严重成角伴明显缩短、或为开放性；查体常见大腿明显水肿、瘀斑、骨擦音和肌肉痉挛，仅骨折局部估计失血就可达约 500-1,500 mL，还有脂肪栓塞的实际风险。处置：监测休克、考虑脊柱防护、建立静脉通路、给予镇痛药，并使用牵引夹板——既能减轻疼痛，又能缩小间室容积、最大限度减少进一步失血。

points.en: Knee fractures (distal femur, proximal tibia, or patella) come from a direct blow, axial load, or a powerful quadriceps contraction — expect pain, reduced range of motion, pain with movement/weight-bearing, ecchymosis, swelling, and (if displaced) deformity. Management hinges on the distal pulse: if intact, splint in the position found; if absent, seek medical consultation before any manipulation. Elevate to heart level, apply cold packs, and reassess neurovascular status frequently given the high rate of compartment syndrome and neurovascular injury with knee fractures. Reminder: a knee injury in an MVC patient should make you specifically look for a posterior hip dislocation, since both come from the same dashboard mechanism.
points.zh: 膝部骨折（股骨远端、胫骨近端或髌骨）源自直接打击、轴向负荷或股四头肌强力收缩——预期表现为疼痛、活动度下降、活动/负重时疼痛加重、瘀斑、肿胀，移位时可见畸形。处置关键看远端脉搏：可及则原位固定；消失则先寻求医疗指导再考虑操作。抬高至心脏水平、冰敷，并鉴于膝部骨折合并筋膜间室综合征和神经血管损伤的比例较高，要频繁复评神经血管状态。提醒：车祸患者若发现膝部损伤，要特别排查是否合并同侧髋关节后脱位，因为两者源自同一「膝撞仪表板」机制。

points.en: Tibia/fibula fractures come from direct trauma or rotational/compressive force and often present with significant deformity and soft-tissue injury; watch for compartment syndrome, neurovascular injury, infection, poor healing, and chronic pain. Treatment: rigid long-leg splint, pain medication, elevation to heart level, cold packs, and frequent monitoring for compartment syndrome; if there's neurovascular compromise or severe angulation, attempt alignment while documenting neurovascular status both before and after.
points.zh: 胫腓骨骨折源自直接外伤或旋转/压缩外力，常表现为明显畸形和软组织损伤；要警惕筋膜间室综合征、神经血管损伤、感染、愈合不良和慢性疼痛。处置：硬质长腿夹板、镇痛药、抬高至心脏水平、冰敷，并频繁监测是否出现筋膜间室综合征；若有神经血管受累或严重成角，可尝试对线，但需在操作前后都记录神经血管状态。

points.en: Ankle fractures come from a sudden forceful foot movement damaging the malleoli (sometimes with a dislocation — a fracture-dislocation) or from an axial load driving the talus into the distal tibia; complications include neurovascular damage to the foot, compartment syndrome, and chronic ankle pain/arthritis. Splint with toes exposed, elevate, give analgesia, apply cold packs. If a fracture-dislocation leaves the foot PULSELESS, medical direction may authorize reduction: flex the knee to relax the calf, grasp the heel and forefoot, apply gentle traction, and rotate the foot back into position without forcing — then reassess and splint in the reduced position, or if it fails, notify medical control/the receiving facility and expedite transport splinted as found. Wear eye protection and a gown whenever manipulating an open fracture, since blood can splash.
points.zh: 踝部骨折源自突然的暴力性足部运动损伤内外踝（有时合并脱位，即骨折脱位），或轴向负荷将距骨撞入胫骨远端；并发症包括足部神经血管损伤、筋膜间室综合征以及慢性踝痛/关节炎。固定时露出脚趾，抬高患肢，给予镇痛，冰敷。若骨折脱位导致足部无脉，医疗指导可能授权复位：先屈膝放松小腿肌肉，握住足跟和前足，施加轻柔牵引，不强行地把足部旋回原位——随后复评并在复位后的位置固定；若复位失败，通知医疗指导和接收医院，按原位固定并加快转运。操作开放性骨折时务必戴护目镜和穿隔离衣，因为可能有血液飞溅。

points.en: Calcaneus fractures classically follow jumping/falling and landing on the feet (axial load), less often a direct blow to the heel — expect foot pain, swelling, ecchymosis, and a mandatory index of suspicion for associated knee, pelvis, and spine injury. Splint with a pillow, apply cold packs, give analgesia, and always apply spinal precautions given the high risk of an associated spine injury — particularly when the fracture is BILATERAL.
points.zh: 跟骨骨折典型见于跳跃或坠落后双脚着地（轴向负荷），较少见于直接撞击足跟——表现为足部疼痛、肿胀、瘀斑，且必须高度怀疑合并膝、骨盆和脊柱损伤。用枕头固定，冰敷，给予镇痛，并鉴于合并脊柱损伤的高风险——尤其是双侧跟骨骨折时——务必采取脊柱防护措施。

sections.titleEn: Joint Injuries: Shoulder Girdle and Upper Extremity

points.en: Acromioclavicular (AC) joint separation follows a direct blow to the point of the shoulder (contact sports, falls) — pain/tenderness at the AC joint with a noticeable prominence of the distal clavicle; sling and swath usually provide significant pain relief.
points.zh: 肩锁（AC）关节分离源自肩部顶端受到直接撞击（接触性运动、跌倒）——AC 关节处疼痛压痛，锁骨远端明显隆起；悬吊带加固定带通常能显著缓解疼痛。

points.en: Posterior sternoclavicular joint dislocation follows a direct blow to the clavicle or strong pressure on the posterior shoulder (e.g. the bottom of a football pileup). The dislocation itself is easy to spot (pain/swelling at the joint), but what makes it dangerous — even potentially fatal — is possible damage to the trachea, esophagus, jugular vein, subclavian vessels, or carotid artery underneath. Danger signs demanding rapid transport: dyspnea, pain on swallowing, a choking sensation, loss of pulses, or a sensory deficit in the same-side arm. Position the patient supine with the affected arm abducted and a rolled towel under the shoulder blade to ease pressure on those underlying structures.
points.zh: 胸锁关节后脱位源自锁骨直接受撞击，或肩后方受到强力挤压（如美式橄榄球叠人堆底部）。脱位本身不难识别（关节处疼痛肿胀），但真正危险——甚至可能致命——的是可能伤及下方的气管、食管、颈静脉、锁骨下血管或颈动脉。需立即快速转运的危险信号：呼吸困难、吞咽痛、窒息感、脉搏消失，或同侧手臂出现感觉缺损。体位应取仰卧、患侧手臂外展，肩胛骨下垫一条卷毛巾以减轻对这些深部结构的压力。

points.en: About 90% of shoulder dislocations are ANTERIOR, typically from a FOOSH with the arm abducted and externally rotated — the arm stays abducted/externally rotated, any attempt to move it is extremely painful, a bulge from the acromion is visible anteriorly, and the humeral head may be palpable. Posterior dislocations are much less common and usually follow massive muscle contraction (electrical shock, seizure) — the arm is held internally rotated and adducted instead. Either type can tear the rotator cuff, fracture the glenoid, or injure the brachial plexus/axillary vessels; specifically check sensation over the deltoid for an axillary nerve deficit. Re-dislocation risk is highest in the first 2 years after injury, especially in young patients.
points.zh: 约 90% 的肩关节脱位是前脱位，典型机制是跌倒手撑地时手臂处于外展外旋位——手臂维持外展外旋，任何活动尝试都极其疼痛，肩前方可见肩峰隆起，肱骨头可触及。后脱位少见得多，通常源自剧烈肌肉收缩（触电、癫痫发作）——此时手臂维持内旋内收位。两种脱位都可能撕裂肩袖、造成关节盂骨折或伤及臂丛神经/腋血管；要特别检查三角肌区感觉以排查腋神经损伤。再次脱位的风险在伤后头 2 年内最高，年轻患者尤其如此。

points.en: Elbow dislocation is a medical emergency because of its high neurovascular-injury risk. The vast majority are posterior, from a FOOSH or elbow hyperextension — expect significant pain/swelling/ecchymosis, a palpable deformity from the prominent olecranon, and locking or resistance to movement. Complications: an associated periarticular fracture, brachial artery injury, median nerve injury, and ulnar nerve injury. Radial head subluxation ('nursemaid's elbow') is NOT a true dislocation — it hits children under 6 after a sudden pull on the arm, the arm is held in flexion, the child refuses to move it, and swelling is only mild.
points.zh: 肘关节脱位属于医疗急症，因其神经血管损伤风险高。绝大多数是后脱位，源自跌倒手撑地或肘关节过度伸展——预期表现为明显疼痛/肿胀/瘀斑、鹰嘴突出形成的可触及畸形、以及关节交锁或活动受限。并发症：合并关节周围骨折、肱动脉损伤、正中神经损伤、尺神经损伤。桡骨头半脱位（「牵拉肘」）不是真正的脱位——多见于 6 岁以下儿童手臂被突然牵拉后，患臂维持屈曲位、患儿拒绝活动，肿胀通常轻微。

points.en: Treatment of shoulder-girdle and elbow dislocations: splint in the position found, using blankets/pillows and sling and swath where applicable — for a dislocated shoulder it may take two cravats linked together to encircle the body, extremity, and supporting pillows. Give pain medication given the likely muscle spasm, and reassess neurovascular status frequently. Transport promptly to an emergency department for reduction and full neurovascular workup.
points.zh: 肩带和肘关节脱位的处置：在原位固定，用毛毯/枕头及悬吊带加固定带（如适用）——肩关节脱位有时需要把两条三角巾连起来才能环绕身体、患肢和支撑用的枕头。考虑到可能出现的肌肉痉挛，应给予镇痛药，并频繁复评神经血管状态。尽快转运至急诊科接受复位和完整的神经血管评估。

points.en: Finger dislocations come from a jamming force or hyperextension beyond normal range, producing pain, deformity at the joint, and possible neurovascular compromise (paraesthesia in the digit). Manage by splinting the whole hand in the position of function with soft dressing support or buddy taping — do NOT attempt reduction in the field without medical-control direction. If directed: extend the digit if it's dislocated dorsally, flex it if dislocated volarly, then apply gentle longitudinal traction (pressure at the dislocated joint can help push the distal part back into place); reassess neurovascular status afterward and fully immobilize to prevent re-dislocation.
points.zh: 手指脱位源自猛烈的顶撞力或超出正常范围的过伸，表现为关节处疼痛、畸形，可能伴神经血管受累（手指感觉异常）。处理方法是把整只手以功能位固定，用软敷料支撑或并指固定——未经医疗指导授权，不要在现场尝试复位。如获授权：背侧脱位则伸展该指，掌侧脱位则屈曲该指，随后施加轻柔纵向牵引（在脱位关节处加压有助于把远端推回原位）；复位后复评神经血管状态，并完全固定以防再次脱位。

sections.titleEn: Joint Injuries: Hip and Knee Dislocations

points.en: More than 90% of hip dislocations are POSTERIOR, typically a deceleration injury where a flexed knee strikes an immovable object (the dashboard mechanism) — the affected leg is found flexed, adducted, internally rotated, and notably shortened. Complications: sciatic nerve injury, avascular necrosis of the femoral head, and an associated acetabular fracture. Anterior hip dislocation follows a forceful spreading injury with the hip flexed — the leg is instead flexed, abducted, and externally rotated — with complications of femoral artery/nerve injury and avascular necrosis of the femoral head.
points.zh: 超过 90% 的髋关节脱位是后脱位，典型机制是减速伤——屈曲的膝部撞上不可移动的物体（如仪表板机制）——患肢表现为屈曲、内收、内旋，并明显缩短。并发症：坐骨神经损伤、股骨头缺血性坏死、合并髋臼骨折。前脱位则源自髋关节屈曲位时受到的强力分离外力——患肢表现为屈曲、外展、外旋——并发症为股动脉/神经损伤和股骨头缺血性坏死。

points.en: Because most hip dislocations involve a high-energy mechanism, do a full trauma assessment with spinal precautions. Splint the injured leg in the position found using blankets, pillows, and the opposite leg for support, and perform and document frequent neurovascular checks — definitive reduction almost always requires general anaesthesia in hospital.
points.zh: 由于多数髋关节脱位涉及高能量机制，应做完整的创伤评估并采取脊柱防护。用毛毯、枕头和健侧腿支撑，在原位固定患肢，并进行并记录频繁的神经血管检查——确定性复位几乎都需要在医院全身麻醉下完成。

points.en: Knee dislocation is a true, limb-threatening emergency — from either high-energy trauma (MVCs) or powerful twisting (an athlete cutting to avoid another player) — and often relocates spontaneously, so there may be NO obvious deformity to find. Direction is described by where the tibia sits relative to the femur: anterior (from hyperextension, the MOST common pattern at almost half of all cases, tears the posterior cruciate ligament, and carries a relatively LOW risk of popliteal artery intimal tear); posterior (a direct blow drives the tibia back, tearing the anterior cruciate ligament and carrying a HIGH risk of popliteal artery injury); medial and lateral (direct blows from the opposite side, injuring the collateral ligament on the stretched side) are less common and carry a lower popliteal-artery risk than posterior dislocations.
points.zh: 膝关节脱位是真正的、威胁肢体的急症——可源自高能量创伤（车祸）或强力扭转（运动员变向躲避对手）——常会自行复位，因此可能完全看不出明显畸形。方向按胫骨相对股骨的位置描述：前脱位（源自过度伸展，是最常见的型态，占近一半病例，撕裂后交叉韧带，腘动脉内膜撕裂风险相对较低）；后脱位（直接打击将胫骨推向后方，撕裂前交叉韧带，腘动脉损伤风险高）；内侧和外侧脱位（对侧受到直接打击，损伤被牵拉一侧的副韧带）较少见，腘动脉风险低于后脱位。

points.en: Knee-dislocation complications include limb-threatening popliteal artery disruption, popliteal/peroneal/tibial nerve injury, and joint instability — do not confuse this with a comparatively minor patellar dislocation. Management hinges entirely on distal neurovascular status: if a foot pulse is palpable, splint the knee in the position found; if there's no palpable pulse, you may need to reduce the knee to restore circulation — factors like time to hospital and how long the dislocation has been present matter, so ALWAYS seek medical direction before attempting it.
points.zh: 膝关节脱位的并发症包括威胁肢体的腘动脉断裂、腘/腓/胫神经损伤和关节不稳——不要把它和相对轻微的髌骨脱位混淆。处置完全取决于远端神经血管状态：若足部脉搏可触及，原位固定膝关节；若脉搏消失，可能需要复位以恢复循环——到院时间、脱位持续时长等因素都会影响决策，所以务必先寻求医疗指导才能尝试复位。

points.en: Knee reduction technique (only with medical direction): one rescuer applies longitudinal traction to the tibia toward the foot while a second applies counter-pressure at the distal femur and proximal tibia — for an anterior dislocation, push the femur anteriorly and the tibia in the opposite direction; for a posterior dislocation, reverse it (tibia pressed anteriorly, femur posteriorly). After reduction, recheck neurovascular status and splint the leg securely; if the attempt fails, splint in the position found and transport rapidly instead.
points.zh: 膝关节复位手法（仅在医疗指导下进行）：一人对胫骨施加朝向足部的纵向牵引，另一人在股骨远端和胫骨近端施加反向压力——前脱位时把股骨推向前方、胫骨推向相反方向；后脱位则相反（胫骨推向前方、股骨推向后方）。复位后复查神经血管状态并牢固固定患肢；若复位失败，则在原位固定并加快转运。
